subject: ParcelFlow: accelerated commit proposal + soft-throttle guardrails
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alec Turner <alec@parcelflow.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: ParcelFlow onboarding — proposal for accelerated monthly commit

Hi Alec —

Great talking last week. As discussed, we've sketched a short path to support ParcelFlow's Q3 volume spike while keeping predictable unit economics for you. Attached is a clean copy of the proposal (ParcelFlow_MA_proposal_v3.pdf) and a simple rateband matrix (parcelflow_rateband_matrix.xlsx). Key points up front: 

- Baseline hosted commit: 2.5M tokens / month, billed monthly.
- Accelerated uplift: immediate opt-in to 5M tokens / month for the initial 3-month window (April–June) to cover peak routing and A/B experiments.
- Burst allowance: 20% burst headroom above committed throughput with soft-throttle policy to preserve latency SLOs; overages billed at tiered rates.
- Rateband discounts apply at thresholds: >=5M tokens qualifies for 12% discount on per-token generation rates; >=10M moves to 18%.
- Canary plan: enable a canary route for 20% of traffic routed to the higher-throughput pool for 7 days before full ramp.

Operational notes:
- We'll provision reserved capacity in us-west and pre-stage cache warming for your top 25 prompt templates (you can share the list in a short CSV).
- We'll expose a per-route soft-throttle flag so you can opt to return partial completions vs. queueing during transient pressure.

If this direction works, we can route the SOW/DocuSign and set procurement expectations. I've included a HubSpot link in the related docs. Can we lock this by Friday so dedicated capacity is in place by May 1?

Thanks —
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0124
Redwood Inference

Attachments: ParcelFlow_MA_proposal_v3.pdf, parcelflow_rateband_matrix.xlsx
From: Alec Turner <alec@parcelflow.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ParcelFlow onboarding — proposal for accelerated monthly commit

Jordan —

Thanks for the proposal and the clear summary. Two quick clarifying questions from procurement and platform engineering before we move to signatures: 

1) Burst + soft-throttle: If we hit burst for sustained periods (say multiple hours), do we get automatic fallbacks to a lower-latency model variant, or would Redwood queue requests? We need predictable tail latency for package tracking pages.
2) Can you confirm the billing cadence on the 3-month accelerated uplift? Procurement prefers a single quarterly invoice rather than three monthly invoices if possible.

Procurement (cc’d) is also asking whether there's any flexibility on the 12% discount for the first month of the uplift while we validate cost vs. value. If we move to a 6-month committed cadence after the initial window, would that change the discount band?

—Alec
Alec Turner
Director, Engineering (Platform) | ParcelFlow
alec@parcelflow.com | +1 (617) 555-8890
Procurement: procurement@parcelflow.com
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alec Turner <alec@parcelflow.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ParcelFlow onboarding — proposal for accelerated monthly commit

On Tue, Apr 20, 2027 at 10:03 AM Alec Turner <alec@parcelflow.com> wrote:
> Jordan —
>
> Thanks for the proposal and the clear summary. Two quick clarifying questions...

Great questions — answered inline below and copied finance/ops notes for transparency:

1) Burst behaviour + fallbacks:
- Primary behavior: soft-throttle will prefer returning partial completions (with a clear "partial" flag) rather than excessive queueing; this keeps 95th percentile tail latency within SLO.
- Automatic model fallback: we can route to a lighter, lower-cost model variant automatically after sustained burst (configurable threshold, default 15 minutes of sustained >80% utilization). Fallback preserves semantics for most calls but we surface a compatibility header so you can detect variant fallbacks in logs.

2) Billing cadence for the 3-month uplift:
- We can consolidate billing into a single quarterly invoice for the uplift period; finance will still break down monthly usage in the invoice line items.

Discount flexibility:
- For a 3-month trial (5M/month) the standard band is 12%. If ParcelFlow commits to a 6-month accelerated cadence (>=5M/month) we can uplift to 15% starting month 2 and retroactively apply the additional discount to month 1.

Operational next steps:
- If procurement signs off on quarterly billing, I'll generate a DocuSign SOW (Deal DL-2026-3897) with the canary and soft-throttle clauses.
- Please attach the top-25 prompt list so our ops team can pre-warm caches.

Proposed call: Thu, Apr 22, 10:00 AM PT to run through SOW and procurement notes. 

If that works, I’ll book and loop in Marissa for contract ops.

Jordan
